questions: Does the oval finish rate stay at 20/20 near 1.65 s, confirming the baseline is stable for the final design?
On the s-bend and slalom, at what progress and lateral error does the first line loss occur, and do the outer sensors read near 1 or near 0 at that step?
Which features of the unseen-track-like bends (tight radius, sign change) most resemble the failing s-bend and slalom sections?

intent: Deliver the proven iteration-0 baseline exactly as the final design, since it is the only configuration that finishes a track reliably (20/20 oval, repeated in iteration 9). No geometry is changed. The Integrator should report the first line-loss step, progress and lateral error on the s-bend and slalom, and the sensor readings at that step, so the bend limit can be attributed to sensing or to the controller. The main expected risk is that the unseen track behaves like the s-bend or slalom and goes off track.
learning: Ten iterations show a sharp local optimum at the baseline. Every geometry change tested either collapsed the oval or cut its finish rate, and the 0.7 kg mass test refuted the damping hypothesis. The bend failures have stayed near progress 0.17 to 0.28 under all geometry, which points to a controller-side or joint geometry-controller limit. The final geometry is the baseline, and any further gain should come from the Integrator's controller work.
rationale: This is the final iteration, and the unseen-track race is scored on whatever design is delivered here, so robustness matters more than a speculative bend gain. Across ten races, the iteration-0 baseline (0.6 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m radius, five sensors at x = 0, ±0.012, ±0.024 m, y = 0.05 m, 12 mm footprint) is the only design that finishes any track. It finished 20/20 on the oval at about 1.65 s, and iteration 9 reproduced it exactly (score 356.57), so the platform is repeatable. The most recent change, mass 0.7 kg (iteration 10), cut oval finishes to 6/20 and the score to 204, so the hypothesis that extra mass damps oscillation is refuted. Every other single or combined lever (lead at y = 0.03 and 0.07 m, footprints of 8 and 16 mm, the ±0.032 m array, body length 0.12 m, and the lighter or narrower drivetrain) either collapsed the oval or reduced its finish rate. The s-bend and slalom never progressed beyond about 0.28 and 0.12 under any geometry, so geometry alone is unlikely to make them complete. I therefore deliver the iteration-0 baseline unchanged. I expect the same behaviour as iteration 9: a repeatable oval finish and a score near 356, with the unseen track the main uncertainty.
